Thanks for the context, Hannah. I’ve run a quick sensitivity: incremental committed spend for +8 A100-equivalent GPUs (12-month equivalent) looks like ~ $1.2M ARR if they choose 12 months, ~ $1.6M ARR on 18 months.

Concession framing I’d support:
- Option A (12m): 20% credit on incremental committed fees applied as a bill credit across first 3 invoice cycles, plus 30 days of free burst credits (up to 50% of monthly reserved baseline).
- Option B (18m): 12% credit on incremental committed fees applied across first 6 invoice cycles, plus 60 days of free burst credits.

Rationale: larger term reduces unit economics hit, so lower upfront credit is fine. We should be explicit with procurement about what counts as "incremental" (only the 8 GPUs, not their existing pool).

Marissa — can you confirm the finance OK for Option A up to a 20% credit? If >20% we need exec sign-off (revenue recognition + concession policy).

If Marissa signs off up to 20%, Rafael can negotiate Option A or B with Skyline. If we need >20% I'll route to Exec for approval (include P&L attachment).
